chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from some of his companions, who raised it to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, concerning:

Concerning a man who was killed and he had two heirs: one of them pardoned, while the other refused to pardon. He عليه السلام said: “If the one who did not pardon wishes to kill, he may kill, and he must return half of the blood-money to the heirs of the slain person against whom retaliation is carried out.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ: the heirs or legal claimants connected to the victim
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood-money compensation due in homicide cases
key_terms.الْمُقَادِ: the one subjected to retaliatory execution
key_terms.فَعَفَا: pardoned the offender and waived the right of retaliation
key_terms.وَلِيَّانِ: two legal heirs or entitled guardians of the slain person
key_terms.يَقْتُلَ: to carry out killing in retaliation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one heir pardons a murderer and another heir demands qisas?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about differing heirs in a case of retaliation for murder. If one heir pardons and another insists on qisas, the one seeking execution may proceed, but half of the diyah must be returned to the heirs of the person upon whom retaliation is carried out.
